newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says Bundesbank reserves to be revalued.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says Bundesbank reserves to be revalued.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday that the Bundesbank's gold reserves should be revalued to put them closer to the market level but stressed that there would be no sales of Bundesbank gold.
"Germany will not sell one ounce of gold," he told a news conference in Bonn.
Gold is currently valued at an average of 144 marks per ounce in the Bundesbank balance sheet, well below the current market price of around 600 marks.
Waigel said that changes to the Bundesbank law necessary to allow the revaluation to take place would be passed ahead of the parliamentary summer break.
A revaluation of the gold held at the central bank will provide the Bundesbank -- and thus Bonn -- with a windfall profit of about 40 billion marks if the current market price were adopted.
But analysts say setting a new book price between the current book level and the current market level is a likely option.

Bonn, desperate to qualify fairly and squarely for European monetary union, is seeking ways to ensure that its budget deficit can be trimmed back to no more than three percent of gross domestic product this year.
It was not immediately clear how the Bundesbank profit could be used to help Germany qualify for EMU, as such one-off gains cannot be used to reduce deficits under EU rules.
Waigel also told the news conference that the ruling coalition planned to discuss further budget measures but gave no details.
